# rust.exe without `bin` builds the binary `cargo run` would: with several
# binaries and no `default-run`, it fails listing them, and with
# `default-run` it builds only that one. `greet` does not compile, so
# building every binary fails.
[!exec:cargo] skip

! bit
stderr 'set `bin`, or `default-run` in Cargo.toml \(available binaries: greet, other\)'
! exists out.txt

cp Cargo.toml.default-run Cargo.toml
bit
stdout 'run ✔ ok'
grep '\Aother\n\z' out.txt

-- BUILD.bit --
app = rust.exe {}

run = exec {
  command = "#{app.path} > out.txt"
  outputs = ["out.txt"]
}
-- Cargo.toml --
[package]
name = "greet"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
-- Cargo.toml.default-run --
[package]
name = "greet"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
default-run = "other"
-- src/main.rs --
fn main() {
    compile_error!("greet is not built");
}
-- src/bin/other.rs --
fn main() {
    println!("other");
}
